To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the phototoxicity to E. coli and to human erythrocyte membranes of the acetylene PHT is oxygen‐dependent, the lethal target in E. coli is the membrane and the cytotoxic radicals are not generated in nitrogen.
phenylheptatriine plus near ultraviolet light (320–400 nm) inactivates Escherichia colicells and hemolyzes human erythrocyte membranes, and that these effects are oxygen‐dependent.
PHT plus NUL hemolyzed erythrocytes, inactivated E. coli cells and formed free radicals in aqueous solutions in an oxygen‐dependent manner.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a phototoxic compound that has a very low toxicity when used without NUV.
a photodynamic reaction in which PHT plus NUIV is cytotoxic in the presence of oxygen.
the phototoxicity and photomutagenicity of a series of acetylenic hydrocarbons, including phenylheptatriynyl (PHT) and phenylheptacetylenyl (PHAC) ethers, in the presence of oxygen.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PHT plus NUIV causes the formation of radicals and the inactivation of E. coli and the hemolysis of human erythrocyte membranes in an oxygen‐dependent fashion.
PHT plus NUIV is a phototoxin which is oxygen‐dependent in its action on the erythrocyte membrane and on E. coli.
the phototoxicity is due to the formation of a reactive oxygen species.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the phototoxicity is due to a reactive species which is produced in air and which is inactivated in nitrogen.

PHT plus NUL photolysis in air generates radicals which are not toxic but do react with oxygen to form a toxic intermediate which is responsible for hemolysis of human erythrocyte membranes and inactivation of the membranes of E. coli cells.
the phototoxicity and photoreactivity of PHT plus UV light is dependent on the presence of oxygen and the formation of radicals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the phototoxicity observed for PHT plus NUIV is due to the production of cytotoxic radicals in the presence of oxygen.
the phototoxicity and photomutagenicity of PHT plus UV are not mediated by the same reactive species.
PHT plus NUL is phototoxic to E. coli and mammalian cells, and that the membrane is a major site of attack.
